items.claim: DNS resolution, record types and DNS routing are not necessary to produce o4's diagram or justify its cache and load-balancing choices. This link makes the entire DNS lesson mandatory beyond the observable's requirements.
items.fix: Remove sd-dns's serves link to o4.

items.claim: O4 requires placing a CDN, but does not require choosing how content is provisioned into it. Push-versus-pull provisioning is enrichment rather than a prerequisite for producing this observable.
items.fix: Remove sd-push-pull-cdn's serves link to o4.

items.claim: A complete classic interview answer can satisfy every o6 rubric area without an API gateway or consistent hashing. These links turn particular architectural options into universal interview requirements.
items.fix: Remove the serves link to o6 from sd-api-gateway and sd-consistent-hashing; retain these topics as enrichment.

items.claim: Three hard prerequisites gate skills their dependent KCs do not need: identifying a SPOF does not require availability arithmetic, defining WebSockets does not require polling, and the payment case's KCs do not use sagas.
items.fix: Move sd-single-points-of-failure → sd-availability-series-parallel and sd-case-payment-system → sd-sagas from requires to suggests. Move sd-websockets → sd-polling-long-polling to suggests and add a direct requires edge from sd-websockets to sd-http.

items.claim: The proposed read-your-writes mechanism, 'invalidating the key before acknowledging the write', is insufficient. A concurrent reader can fetch the old database value before the write commits and refill the cache after invalidation, allowing the writer's next read to return stale data.
items.fix: Replace the invalidation example with: 'Read-your-writes requires an authoritative read path that has applied the user's write, or version-aware cache reads and fills that reject older versions; cache deletion alone does not guarantee it.'

items.claim: 'Each message in a queue is delivered to exactly one of the consumers' incorrectly implies that a message cannot reach another consumer on redelivery. This conflicts with the later at-least-once delivery lesson.
items.fix: Replace the statement with: 'Competing consumers share the work rather than each receiving a broadcast copy. An unacknowledged message may be redelivered, possibly to another consumer, so processing must tolerate duplicates.'

items.claim: 'No acknowledged write is lost if the leader dies' requires more than acknowledgment from an arbitrary follower. The acknowledged copy must survive durably, and failover must preserve it rather than promoting a lagging replica.
items.fix: State: 'Synchronous replication waits for the configured replica acknowledgments before acknowledging the client. Acknowledged writes survive leader failure when a durable acknowledged copy survives and failover preserves that copy; latency and write availability depend on the required acknowledgment set.'

items.claim: Every timed mock is allotted 40 minutes, while kc-mock-full-attempt requires an uninterrupted 45-minute submission followed by separate review. None of these allocations can accommodate the course's own assessment protocol.
items.fix: Set est_min to 55 for each of the five mocks, allocating 45 minutes to the attempt and 10 minutes to scoring and self-review.

items.claim: The chosen fork promises 10+ case studies, but only four distinct case studies are mandatory; the remaining nine are optional. The required path therefore does not establish completion of the advertised case-study breadth.
items.fix: Add a core completion requirement to finish any six additional distinct case studies alongside the four mandatory classics; do not count mocks of the same systems as additional case studies.

items.claim: The mock requires 'non-guessable codes', but the taught generator only guarantees uniqueness and explicitly permits counter ranges. Unique sequential codes remain predictable, so the learner has no taught mechanism for satisfying this requirement.
items.fix: Add a URL-shortener KC distinguishing uniqueness from unpredictability and teaching sufficiently long cryptographically random codes with atomic collision handling. Require the mock's generator choice to explain how it meets the non-guessability requirement.

items.claim: 'A cached value is never more than one TTL older than the write that produced it' conflates cache residence time with source-data freshness. TTL does not establish a freshness bound when a stale replica or delayed concurrent read supplies the cached value.
items.fix: Replace it with: 'A fixed TTL limits an entry's residence time since insertion or refresh. Bounding staleness relative to source writes additionally requires assumptions about source freshness and concurrent cache fills.'
